subject: Reserved commit term & onboarding calendar for CloudSolv Dedicated
messages_1_subject: Questions on Dedicated reserved commits and start date
messages_1_body:
Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Marcus and I talked through the throughput numbers and we like the Dedicated approach. Before we proceed we'd like clarity on two things so we can align procurement: 

1) Term: your quoting includes 12/24/36-month reserved commits. Can you share the net-effective pricing (after tier discounts) for 12 vs 24 vs 36 month for the 4-GPU and 12-GPU pool profiles? We need simple units (USD per vGPU-hour or per token equivalent) we can put in our finance model.

2) Capacity start / ramp: our Q2 product launch is mid-April. We may need the Dedicated pool to be live earlier than the start-of-month in your standard onboarding. What flexibility is there for a mid-month capacity start & an accelerated ramp to full commit within 6 weeks? Any implications for pricing or pro-rated billing?

If helpful, I can add our procurement lead to the thread.

Best,
Elena
Operations Lead, CloudSolv

P.S. please attach the onboarding calendar and the same proposal you showed with the discount tiers.
messages_2_subject: Re: Questions on Dedicated reserved commits and start date
messages_2_body:
Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up-front and I'll attach a short matrix + onboarding calendar.

Term & net pricing: we publish list rates per GPU-hour; for reserved commits we apply step discounts based on term and commit size. Attached PDF has three example profiles for the 4-GPU and 12-GPU pools showing list, committed discount, and net effective USD per GPU-hour plus an illustrative token-cost conversion for text gen workloads.

Mid-month start & ramp: yes, we can accommodate a mid-month capacity start. Two points to note:
- Billing: first partial month is pro-rated for the days active at list, then committed pricing applies starting on the first full billing cycle after start (we can also apply the commit discount from day one if procurement requests it — that requires accounting approval and a signed SOW that specifies the pro-rate approach).
- Ramp: we support staged pool growth. Standard ramp is 8 weeks; we can compress to 4–6 weeks if we can commit to a firm calendar and weekly check-ins. There is a one-time accelerated onboarding fee if we need to schedule dedicated engineer time earlier than our standard queue.

I've attached a proposed onboarding-calendar.xlsx with a 4-week compressed ramp (milestones: infra prep, network validation, model placement, smoke tests, cutover). Dev has added throughput guardrails which I'll let him expand on below.

If it helps, Marissa and I can provide a pricing sheet with two flavors: (A) discount applied from day one inclusive of pro-rate, (B) discount applied only from first full billing cycle. Which would you prefer for procurement modeling?

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
messages_3_subject: Re: Questions on Dedicated reserved commits and start date
messages_3_body:
Hi Elena — quick technical context on the pool sizing & throughput guarantees you asked about.

1) 4-GPU pool (NVIDIA A100-equivalent):
- Target throughput: ~35–45 concurrent short requests (~8–16 tokens avg) with P95 latency ~180–250ms depending on model and batching policy.
- Good for lower QPS, predictable latency SLOs.

2) 12-GPU pool:
- Target throughput: ~110–140 concurrent short requests with P95 latency ~160–220ms. Better for higher bursty loads.

3) Throughput guarantees & fallbacks:
- We provide committed throughput targets in the SLO appendix; if utilization exceeds expected synthetic load during onboarding, we can define an auto-burst policy (additional pre-warmed capacity at an incremental rate) or an agreed fallback to a compatible quantized model variant.

4) Ramp ops:
- For accelerated ramps we require network validation & IAM keys a minimum of 10 business days before the first capacity activation.
- We'll create an environment-specific test harness and share logs to validate token-rate performance weekly.

Happy to run a joint load test with your infra team during week 2 of the compressed ramp.

—Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
messages_4_subject: Discount structuring & approval path — CloudSolv proposal
messages_4_body:
Hi Elena — looping in procurement/finance expectations.

We ran the numbers and here's the offer we can take to approval: 
- 12-month: 8% off committed list for 4-GPU, 10% off for 12-GPU
- 24-month: 14% off for 4-GPU, 18% off for 12-GPU
- 36-month: 20% off for 4-GPU, 26% off for 12-GPU

If you want the discount applied from day one (pro-rate for partial first month), we need a signed SOW + PO at contract execution. If the PO comes later and you prefer discount from first full billing cycle, that's also standard and doesn't need special approval.

We can also lock a two-step price protection clause if you choose 24 or 36 months — price won't increase for the first 12 months after signing.

Aisha, can you confirm payment terms and whether we can accept a Net 60 PO from CloudSolv with an initial deposit?

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
messages_5_subject: Re: Discount structuring & approval path — CloudSolv proposal
messages_5_body:
Hi Elena — quick procurement note from finance: 

We can accept Net 60 for enterprise customers with an initial 25% deposit on the committed annual value. For 36-month deals we prefer a milestone invoice schedule (yearly in advance or quarterly).

For the mid-month start: we'll put the pro-rate approach into the SOW (two options as Jonas mentioned). If you need the discount from day one, please ensure the PO references the SOW and is signed at contract execution — that prevents the accounting gap.

Next steps I suggest:
- Jonas to share the final proposal PDF with the 3-term pricing table and the onboarding-calendar.xlsx (attached).
- CloudSolv to indicate preferred term (12/24/36) and whether you want discounts effective immediately or from first full billing cycle.
- If you pick accelerated ramp, we'll schedule the network validation call (Dev & CloudSolv infra) for the first available slot in the attached calendar.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
